sourceCopy.examplesHeading: Four useful ways to get started

examples.heading: A simpler pair
examples.text: 12:18 reduces to 2:3 by dividing both terms by 6. The relative amounts remain unchanged.

examples.heading: Find the fourth term
examples.text: 2:3 = 4:? gives 6. Both ratios have the exact value 2/3.

examples.heading: Three exact decimal terms
examples.text: 0.5:1.25:2 becomes 2:5:8. Clearing decimal denominators avoids rounding the relationship.

examples.heading: Double every amount
examples.text: Scaling 2:3:5 by 2 gives 4:6:10. Each term receives the same multiplier.

steps.heading: Choose the question
steps.text: Select the mode that matches the task. The field labels change with the question.

steps.heading: Enter your values
steps.text: Separate ratio terms with a colon. In A:B = C:D, replace exactly one value with ?. Use a dot for decimals.

steps.heading: Read the working
steps.text: Calculate, check the result and inspect the steps. Copy the answer or download the complete result.

method.heading: The rules behind the result
paragraphs: A ratio compares quantities in a fixed order. The pair 2:3 means two parts of the first quantity for three parts of the second. Reversing the terms gives a different relationship. Keep the labels and units in the same order throughout your calculation.

To simplify a ratio of integers, divide every term by their greatest common divisor. A ratio of decimals is first converted into exact fractions. Their denominators are cleared together, then the resulting integer terms are reduced. No decimal rounding is needed.

A multi-term ratio follows the same process. For example, 0.5:1.25:2 becomes 2:5:8. The calculator accepts any practical number of colon-separated terms. An all-zero ratio has no unique simplest form, so it is rejected explicitly.

A proportion A:B = C:D states that A/B equals C/D. Cross-multiplication gives A × D = B × C. Put a question mark in exactly one field. The calculator rearranges the cross-product equation to solve that position, then shows the completed proportion.

The denominator terms B and D cannot be zero in this fraction interpretation. Some other zero combinations also fail to determine a unique missing value. The page reports the undefined division rather than manufacturing a number from a degenerate proportion.

Scaling multiplies every ratio term by the same factor. It does not simplify the result automatically, because the scaled amounts may be the quantities you actually need. A zero scale produces zero quantities; it does not claim that the new all-zero ratio preserves a meaningful fraction.

uses.heading: Use the result with the right context
paragraphs: Use simplified ratios to compare mixtures, share quantities or check an exercise. Convert incompatible units before entering terms. A ratio of centimetres to metres can look wrong if the units are not made consistent first.

Use Scale when you want actual new amounts, such as doubling every part of a recipe. If a recipe contains three ingredients, enter three terms in their original order. The working shows the same multiplier applied to each term.

Use Find a missing value for a direct proportion. An inverse proportion is a different model and is not inferred automatically. Decide whether one amount should rise or fall with the other before treating a real-world problem as A:B = C:D.

privacy.heading: Private calculations, clear limits
paragraphs: Your inputs and results stay in this browser. Calculation runs in a local worker, without a calculation API or uploaded data.
The page saves only your theme preference. A copied link contains the selected inputs and options, so share it deliberately.
Large calculations depend on device time and memory. Cancel stops the active job. An error clears old answers and disables their downloads.

faq.question: How do I enter several terms?
faq.answer: Separate them with colons, such as 2:3:5. Simplify and Scale support more than two terms within your device memory.

faq.question: Can ratio terms be decimals?
faq.answer: Yes. A decimal point is accepted and converted to an exact fraction. The simplification clears denominators before reducing the integers.

faq.question: How do I find a missing term?
faq.answer: Choose Find a missing value. Enter three numbers and place ? in exactly one of A, B, C or D.

faq.question: Can the unknown be in any position?
faq.answer: Yes. The calculator rearranges the cross-product equation for A, B, C or D and checks the completed proportion.

faq.question: Why is an all-zero ratio rejected?
faq.answer: There is no unique reduced relationship when every term is zero. At least one nonzero term is needed for simplification.

faq.question: Can B or D be zero?
faq.answer: Not in A/B = C/D. Those denominator positions must be nonzero, or the proportion is undefined.

faq.question: Does Scale also simplify the result?
faq.answer: No. It multiplies each quantity by the selected factor and keeps the scaled amounts. Choose Simplify when reduction is the task.

faq.question: Does order matter?
faq.answer: Yes. A:B and B:A refer to opposite relationships. Keep your quantity labels in a consistent order.

faq.question: Is this for inverse proportion too?
faq.answer: The missing-value mode solves direct proportions only. An inverse relationship needs a different model and is not guessed from the numbers.

faq.question: Why is a result shown as a fraction?
faq.answer: The exact missing value may not have a terminating decimal. Its fraction stays exact; the decimal panel gives a rounded companion.
